page: Microsoft Azure NC32ads_A10_v4 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for graphics rendering, artificial intelligence inference, and high-performance compute workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture using AMD processors, the instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It integrates dual NVIDIA A10 graphics processing units delivering a total of 48 GB of GPU memory across the paired accelerators.

System resources include 400.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 12.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage architecture features 3092 GB of integrated local SSD space alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The combination of substantial system memory, local high-capacity solid-state storage, and dedicated accelerator memory addresses data-intensive pipelines that process intermediate datasets locally while offloading compute-intensive kernels to the graphics processing units.

From an infrastructure perspective, the server balances processing, memory density, and acceleration capability within a single deployment. Omitting complimentary public IPv4 addresses, it relies on virtual network interfaces for external and internal traffic routing. With 48 GB of aggregate VRAM across two GPUs paired with 32 processor threads, the instance suits workloads such as deep learning inference, video transcoding, visual workstation virtualization, and graphics-heavy simulation tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure NC32ads_A10_v4 is a GPU-accelerated cloud server featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD x86_64 processor and managed under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system incorporates two NVIDIA A10 GPUs offering 48 GB of aggregate video memory. Complementing the visual and compute acceleration hardware, the configuration provides 400.0 GB of system RAM, representing 12.5 GB per vCPU, as well as 3092 GB of high-speed local SSD storage with Azure Premium Storage capability. The high ratio of host RAM to vCPU alongside substantial local solid-state capacity enables efficient handling of extensive working datasets without frequent network disk access. Lacking complimentary public IPv4 addresses, network connectivity is configured within dedicated virtual networks. The instance is suited for deep learning inference, 3D visualization, video processing, scientific simulations, and virtual workstation environments.
